blogs.title: Deference Reaffirmed: The D.C. Circuit’s Easy Path to Exemption 7(A) in National-Security Files
blogs.description: This post unpacks how the court doubled down on a deferential approach to FOIA Exemption 7(A) in counterterrorism investigations. Relying on CREW, CNSS, and Juarez, the panel held that the FBI’s attestation to an ongoing investigation—supplemented by ex parte detail—sufficed to show disclosure could interfere with pending or reasonably anticipated proceedings. We analyze how the opinion treats the FBI’s status as a law-enforcement agency, the required ‘rational nexus’ showing, and why the court did not require a separate “foreseeable harm” analysis post-FOIA Improvement Act in light of 7(A)’s built-in interference standard.

blogs.title: When FOIA Records Grow Old: Managing Staleness Through Updated Declarations
blogs.description: The district court’s insistence on refreshed declarations is the procedural pivot in this case. This post explores the court’s staleness concerns, the FBI’s Bender ‘update,’ and the D.C. Circuit’s choice to read that update in tandem with the earlier, more detailed Hardy submissions. We assess how CREW’s warning about “vague” assertions plays out here, what makes an update adequate, and practical guidance for litigants seeking or resisting periodic refreshes as FOIA suits drag on.

blogs.title: Segregability After Perioperative: Why 10,750 Pages and 80 CDs Yielded “No Meaningful Information”
blogs.description: Focusing on segregability, this post examines the court’s reliance on Mead’s ‘meaningful information’ standard and Perioperative’s approval of ex parte showings to sustain large-scale withholdings. We discuss why line-by-line scrubbing was deemed unreasonable, how categorical 7(A) withholdings intersect with segregability, and what plaintiffs can do—request in camera review, challenge category definitions, or demand fuller public explanations—when agencies say the non-exempt nuggets are too scattered to matter.

blogs.title: FOIA as Not-Discovery: The Farahi Case at the Intersection of Immigration and Counterterrorism
blogs.description: This post situates Farahi in the broader tension between FOIA transparency and ongoing enforcement in removal and counterterrorism contexts. We consider how allegations aired in immigration proceedings (e.g., ties to designated terrorist organizations) fed the Exemption 7(A) analysis, why FOIA cannot be used to pry loose investigative files midstream, and what this means for noncitizens seeking their records while parallel enforcement actions—criminal or administrative—remain live.
